name: Halo laser (hybrid fractional)
lead: Halo is a hybrid fractional laser, a category that combines an ablative and a non-ablative fractional wavelength in a single pass, aimed at photoaging, scars and pigment. Source material for this entry is thin, consisting of clinical trial registrations that name the Profile Halo mixed fractional laser or hybrid fractional lasers generally [1][2].

Registered studies are small: a 15-person study of facial and neck photoaging with the Profile Halo [1], a 34-person study of various skin conditions including dyschromia and photodamage [2], and a trial of a hybrid fractional laser for acne scars in skin of color [3].
infobox: Photoaging, dyschromia, acne scars, skin laxity

paras: A completed study registered in 2015 evaluated the Profile Halo mixed fractional laser for facial and neck photoaging in 15 participants [1]. A completed 2016 study (n=34) addressed dyschromia and photodamaged skin [2]. A 2019 study tested a hybrid fractional laser on off-face skin laxity in 7 participants [4], and a recruiting trial from 2023 (n=50) examines acne scars with pigmentation risk in skin of color [3]. Results are not reported in the registrations used here, and no larger controlled evidence is cited.

card.summary: A hybrid ablative/non-ablative fractional laser for photoaging and scars; only small registered studies are cited.
card.note: Thin sourcing; trial results not summarised.

quick.overview:
Halo is a hybrid fractional laser used in clinics for skin texture, tone, photoaging and scarring, combining two laser modes in one treatment.

Only small trials are registered.
quick.mechanism: Hybrid fractional systems deliver both ablative and non-ablative microscopic columns of laser injury to prompt skin remodeling.
quick.risks: Hyperpigmentation after laser treatment is a studied concern, particularly in darker skin tones [3]. Downtime depends on settings and is not detailed in the sources used here.
